IN PHOTOS | Barbed-wire fences are installed by the Manila Police District near the Mendiola Peace Arch in Manila on Friday, November 14, 2025, in preparation for the upcoming November 30 protest.

The Philippine National Police cautioned protesters that stricter security protocols will be in place and said it will not tolerate any violence, as authorities brace for a potentially massive anti-corruption rally following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s appeal for a peaceful demonstration ahead of the “Trillion Peso March” sequel.

📷 Norman Cruz

For more info, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSgGa.

LOOK: In New York City, progressive groups led by BAYAN USA Northeast held a protest outside the Philippine Consulate to criticize government corruption and inaction. The groups said these issues worsen the impact of disasters like the recent Typhoons Tino and Uwan.

Bayan called on fellow Filipinos abroad to hold leaders accountable and demand justice for those affected. 

The protest, held on Nov. 8,  also remembered the 12th anniversary of Super Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda), one of the deadliest storms that hit the Philippines.

There’s a version of Web3 that doesn’t care about speculation or hype cycles.

It just wants to work when the stakes are high.

@VenomFoundation was built for that version.

It isn’t chasing retail excitement but building for systems that need consistency.

Things like payments, tokenized assets or digital currencies that fail quietly if you get them wrong.

Its basis is “dynamic sharding” when traffic spikes.

The network automatically splits and balances load.

No congestion drama, just real-time elasticity.

Then comes its “Threaded Virtual Machine”.

It’s not about reinventing smart contracts, it’s about running them in parallel.

That design removes global bottlenecks and keeps fees near zero.

Venom’s architecture is layered on purpose.

It carries identity, KYC, and compliance logic at the protocol level.

The $VENOM token tells the same story: technical strength and early traction.

It trades around $0.06, with roughly 38% of supply unlocked and liquidity still thin.

Real movements are already in motion:

➠ The Philippines is testing government digitalization.

➠ The UAE is running carbon credit systems.

➠ There’s talk of deeper infrastructure partnerships in Asia.

Slow, serious moves, not noise.

Web3 doesn’t only need chains that move fast.

It also needs chains that stay reliable when it matters and venom looks like the answer to that problem.

In addition to this, creators can also join the @BingXOfficial blaster program for Venom and get a share of the $9K prize pool: https://t.co/f5GNuEk1vL

And if you’re new to BingX, you can sign up with my invite code: RECPDA.

#BingXSpotBlast for the culture 🤝

🚨🚨🚨⚡

𝐀 𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐨 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐮𝐝𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐫𝐞 𝐛𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐬𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞 𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐬. 

Elizaldy Co himself admits it: ₱100 billion was inserted into the 2025 budget, and he did so under the instruction of President Bongbong Marcos and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Half to DPWH.
Half to unprogrammed funds.
𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐃𝐁𝐌 𝐒𝐞𝐜. 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐡 𝐏𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐧, 𝐏𝐋𝐋𝐎 𝐔𝐬𝐞𝐜. 𝐀𝐝𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐧, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐎𝐉 𝐔𝐬𝐞𝐜. 𝐉𝐨𝐬𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐳.

Then the darker part:
That the administration is using the full machinery of the state to keep him silent.

Threats. Pressure. And the fear that he will be turned into panakip-butas in a manufactured anti-corruption narrative.

₱100 billion is not an accident. It is a choice.

But in the end, maybe this story can only cross from allegation to truth if he returns to the Philippines and testifies to all of this himself.

ctto: #RegalOliva
📸 PhilStar
